# Part A: Data Exploration & Initial Modeling

## Distributions of $Y$ and predictors

```{r}
#| label: fig-distributions
#| fig-cap: "Distributions of the response and quantitative predictors."

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
hist(dat$y,  main = "Y",  xlab = "y")
hist(dat$x1, main = "X1", xlab = "x1")
hist(dat$x2, main = "X2", xlab = "x2")
```

_Comments on shape, skew, and unusual values._

## Relationships with $Y$

```{r}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Response versus each quantitative predictor."

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(y ~ x1, data = dat)
plot(y ~ x2, data = dat)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-boxplot
#| fig-cap: "Response by level of the categorical predictor."

boxplot(y ~ grp, data = dat)
```

_Comments: linear? curved? does spread change with $X$?_

## Outliers and extreme values

_Which observations look unusual, and do we have a reason to keep or remove them?_

## Transformations

If $Y$ is right-skewed or the variance grows with the mean, consider $\log(Y)$ or $\sqrt{Y}$.
If the relationship is curved, consider adding a quadratic term:

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i + \beta_2 X_i^2 + \varepsilon_i
$$

_Our decision and reasoning._

## Correlation & multicollinearity

```{r}
#| label: correlation

num_vars <- dat[, c("y", "x1", "x2")]
round(cor(num_vars), 2)
pairs(num_vars)
```

The variance inflation factor for predictor $j$ is

$$
\text{VIF}_j = \frac{1}{1 - R_j^2},
$$

where $R_j^2$ comes from regressing $X_j$ on the other predictors. Values above about 10 suggest serious multicollinearity.

_Comments._

## Simple linear regressions

Model: $Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_i + \varepsilon_i$, with $\varepsilon_i \overset{iid}{\sim} N(0, \sigma^2)$.

```{r}
#| label: slr

slr1 <- lm(y ~ x1, data = dat)
summary(slr1)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-slr-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostic plots for the simple linear regression of Y on X1."

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(slr1)
```

**Assumption checks:**

- Linearity: _residuals vs. fitted_
- Constant variance: _scale-location plot_
- Normality: _Q-Q plot_
- Independence: _how the data were collected_

**Remedies, if needed:** _..._

# Part B: Deeper Analysis

## Candidate multiple regression models

$$
Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i1} + \beta_2 X_{i2} + \beta_3 \,\mathbb{1}\{\text{grp}_i = \text{B}\} + \varepsilon_i
$$

```{r}
#| label: mlr

mlr1 <- lm(y ~ x1 + x2 + grp, data = dat)
summary(mlr1)

# VIF (needs the car package: install.packages("car"))
if (requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE)) car::vif(mlr1)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-mlr-diagnostics
#| fig-cap: "Diagnostic plots for the candidate multiple regression model."

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
plot(mlr1)
```

## Interactions

_Does the effect of $X_1$ depend on group? Example model:_

```{r}
#| label: interaction

mlr_int <- lm(y ~ x1 * grp + x2, data = dat)
summary(mlr_int)
anova(mlr1, mlr_int)   # partial F-test: is the interaction needed?
```

## Model comparison

| Model | Predictors | $R^2_{adj}$ | AIC | Notes |
|-------|------------|-------------|-----|-------|
| SLR | $X_1$ |  |  |  |
| MLR 1 | $X_1, X_2$, grp |  |  |  |
| MLR + interaction | $X_1 \times$ grp, $X_2$ |  |  |  |
